methodological_rigor.justification: The study design is strong for the question posed: longitudinally paired indolent/active T-PLL scRNA-seq in 11 patients plus 6 singletons (28 samples, 204,959 cells), complemented by WGS on 3 paired patients, plus orthogonal validation using qRT-PCR, Western blot, flow cytometry, and Seahorse bioenergetic assays. Statistical rigor is solid with permutation testing (B=10,000), FDR correction, pairwise Wilcoxon/MWW tests, edgeR-LRT pseudo-bulk DE, and validation in two independent bulk cohorts (n=69 and n=48). Limitations acknowledged include no predetermined sample size, no randomization or blinding, and inability to do robust global pseudotime due to inter-patient heterogeneity; age was controlled by design rather than adjustment, which is a defensible but imperfect choice. Multi-center sampling (six centers) strengthens generalizability for a rare disease, though WGS is under-powered at n=3 pairs.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: As a longitudinal descriptive/correlative case series of 17 treatment-naive T-PLL patients with single-cell transcriptomic and limited WGS profiling, this maps to Oxford LoE 4 (case series / low-quality cohort). Clinical relevance is plausible but not demonstrated: findings implicate MYC inhibitors, CDK inhibitors, CD47/SIRPα axis, and KIR3DL2 as conceptual therapeutic targets, and the authors note these have not been tested in T-PLL. The translational path is credible given T-PLL's dismal 24-month median survival and the paucity of disease-specific therapies, but no intervention, outcome, or biomarker is prospectively validated here.

reporting_quality.justification: As an observational longitudinal study with translational wet-lab components, STROBE is the most applicable framework, though no reporting checklist is explicitly cited aside from the Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary referenced in Methods. Methods are thorough: patient eligibility, consensus classification criteria, ethics approvals (Cologne #11-319; Vienna 1957/2020), sample handling, sequencing parameters (28,280 reads/cell average, 44.99x WGS coverage), software versions, and analytic thresholds are all specified. Data availability is strong: a GitHub/Zenodo deposit (10.5281/zenodo.17568926) is cited for code, bulk cohorts are re-used from GEO GSE214284 and published sources, and supplementary data tables are referenced; raw scRNA/WGS deposition accessions are not explicitly quoted in the main text excerpt but a reporting summary is linked.

novelty_literature.justification: T-PLL is a rare aggressive mature T-cell leukemia with scant molecular data, and this is the first single-cell transcriptomic dissection of the indolent-to-active transition using intra-patient longitudinal sampling, paired with longitudinal WGS. The identification of MYC-signature amplification with coupled metabolic activation, ATM clonal outgrowth, progressive TCR-signaling attenuation (including recurrent PTPRC/CD45 loss in 4/11), and reduced tumor-microenvironment cross-talk represents a meaningful mechanistic extension rather than a first-in-class discovery, since MYC and ATM involvement in T-PLL were previously reported (refs 13, 35, 46). The novelty lies in the longitudinal paired-stage design in an under-studied disease, which fills a documented gap; guarding against novelty leniency, the individual mechanistic insights are incremental rather than paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear narrative arc from transcriptomic atlas through MYC/metabolism, TCR signaling attenuation, and microenvironment remodeling, culminating in a proposed five-step progression model (Fig. 7). Figure legends are detailed, statistical annotations are explicit (tests, p-values, effect sizes, CIs where appropriate), and hedged language is used appropriately for preliminary findings. Some passages in the Discussion are dense and could be tightened, and the large number of supplementary figures referenced may burden readers, but overall clarity, structure, and scientific prose quality are high.

key_strengths: Rare longitudinal intra-patient indolent/active paired scRNA-seq (11 pairs) in T-PLL, enabled by six-center collaboration on an ultra-rare disease

Convergent multi-modal validation: scRNA-seq cross-validated against two independent bulk T-PLL cohorts (n=69 and n=48), qRT-PCR (Pearson r=0.95), Western blot, flow cytometry, and Seahorse functional bioenergetics
Longitudinal WGS on three paired patients directly demonstrates ATM allele-frequency outgrowth (69.8% to 91.3%) and MYC 8q gains coupling genomics to transcriptomic MYC signatures
Rigorous statistics with permutation testing (B=10,000), FDR control, pseudo-bulk edgeR-LRT, and age/sex controlled by study design
Concrete translational implications articulated with appropriate humility (MYC inhibitors, CDK inhibitors, CD47/SIRPα, KIR3DL2)
key_concerns: Small WGS cohort (n=3 pairs) and modest overall patient number (n=17) limit statistical power for genomic associations and preclude subgroup analyses
Observational design with no intervention or outcome endpoint; therapeutic targets remain conceptual and untested in T-PLL
No explicit STROBE or reporting-standard checklist cited in the text, and raw-data accession numbers are not clearly visible in the main text excerpt
Global pseudotime could not be robustly inferred due to inter-patient heterogeneity, limiting cross-patient trajectory claims
Some mechanistic claims (e.g., NicheNet-derived ligand candidates, ANXA1/CD48) are acknowledged as preliminary and require dedicated functional follow-up
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a methodologically solid, novel longitudinal single-cell dissection of T-PLL progression in a rare and lethal disease with strong multi-modal validation, but it is a descriptive/correlative case series (LoE 4) without prospective clinical validation of targets, making it an excellent fit for a Tier 2 journal (e.g., Nature Communications-type) with minor revisions to strengthen reporting-standard compliance and data-deposition visibility.
